meta.title: Specialisation Pages + Supporting Content Cluster
meta.scope: Combined Phase 6 and Phase 7. Includes dedicated specialisation pages and the supporting intent-driven content architecture required around course, university-course and comparison pages.
meta.critical_confirmation: YES — dedicated specialisation pages are explicitly included in this phase.
meta.architecture: Course Pillar → Specialisation Hub → University/Course Pages → Comparison → Supporting Articles/Guides
meta.goal: Capture deeper search intent without creating thin keyword pages, while keeping every specialisation fact tied to verified university/course data.

phase_6_specialisation_pages.purpose: Create dedicated, useful specialisation pages only where the specialisation has real programme-level demand and verified university offerings.
phase_6_specialisation_pages.core_rule: A specialisation page is an intent page, not a copied university-course page. It explains the specialisation, subjects, skills, career directions and which universities actually offer it.
do_not_create: A page for every possible keyword variation.
A page when only one university offers the specialisation unless the intent is genuinely strong and the page has sufficient unique value.
A page merely by replacing the specialisation name inside the same generic template.
A page for a specialisation that is not verified in the current programme data.

specialisation_page_structure.content: Specialisation name + course + concise definition + who it suits + current-session verification.
Original plain-language explanation, scope and how it differs from the broader course.
Background, interests, career direction and learning expectations.
Common subject areas as an explanatory layer. Then show verified university-specific subjects/electives in a clearly labelled table.
Dynamic cards sourced from verified university-course records.
Do not invent a specialisation fee. Show university-specific programme fees and note when the specialisation is included within the programme fee.
Explain the course-level rule, then show university-specific differences.
Explain only verified programme-level assessment information.
Skill families tied to the curriculum rather than generic job claims.
Role families, typical responsibilities and skills to build. No salary or placement guarantees.
Useful comparisons such as Finance vs Marketing or Data Science vs AI only when both pages/paths exist.

specialisation_page_structure.section: How to choose a university for this specialisation
specialisation_page_structure.content: Curriculum fit, electives, faculty/support, fees, exams, projects and career support.
Link to the relevant course comparison experience with the specialisation as the decision filter where supported.
Contextual action such as Explore universities offering this specialisation or Compare available programmes.

specialisation_seo.title_pattern: {Specialisation} Online — Syllabus, Subjects, Fees, Universities & Career Options 2026-27
specialisation_seo.h1_pattern: Online {Specialisation}: Syllabus, Subjects, Universities & Career Options
specialisation_seo.meta_pattern: Explore Online {Specialisation}: subjects, syllabus, eligibility, fees, universities, skills, career options and programme comparison for 2026-27.
schema: FAQPage only for visible valid FAQs
specialisation_seo.indexation: Index only when the page has substantial unique content and verified university availability.
specialisation_seo.thin_page_rule: If there is insufficient unique evidence/content, do not index a thin page. Keep the specialisation discoverable through the course pillar instead.

specialisation_internal_linking.specialisation_to_university_course: Specialisation page → exact university-course pages that offer it.
specialisation_internal_linking.specialisation_to_comparison: Specialisation → course comparison filtered/positioned around relevant options where technically supported.

specialisation_generation_workflow: Extract all verified specialisation names from the university-course data layer.
Normalize spelling and slug format without changing official programme names.
Group equivalent names only when they genuinely represent the same academic area; preserve official names on university cards.
Count how many universities offer each specialisation.
Assess search intent and unique informational value.
Create an indexable page only when the threshold is met.
Populate the university availability list from verified records.
Write original explanation and decision guidance.
Attach official sources and last verified date.

publish_only_if: Specialisation is verified in at least one current programme source.
Page contains meaningful unique content beyond a university list.
No generic curriculum is presented as universal.
Actual electives are clearly labelled as university-specific.
Career content is skill/role based and non-guaranteed.

phase_7_supporting_content_cluster.purpose: Build supporting articles/guides around real search intent and connect them into the course, specialisation, university-course and comparison architecture.
content_types: News/update where there is a genuinely time-sensitive event
article_structure: Common mistakes or things to verify

article_seo.title_rule: Write for the actual question, not keyword stuffing.
article_seo.meta: Accurately describe the article; no clickbait.
article_seo.canonical: Self-canonical unless the article is intentionally consolidated.
schema: FAQPage only when visible FAQs genuinely exist
article_seo.images: Use descriptive alt text; do not use keyword-stuffed alt attributes.
article_seo.freshness: Update facts when they change; do not change dates simply to look fresh.

source_hierarchy: Competitor pages only for gap analysis and search-intent discovery, never as factual authority
content_research_workflow: Identify what existing website content already covers.
Research competing pages only to discover gaps and structure.
Add internal links to the appropriate pillar/specialisation/university-course/comparison page.
Check factual claims and source freshness.

anti_cannibalization_matrix.rule: If two pages answer essentially the same question, consolidate or clearly differentiate them before publishing.

internal_linking_rules: Every article should have a clear parent topic.
Link upward to the relevant course pillar.
Link sideways to a relevant specialisation or comparison page when useful.
Link downward to exact university-course pages only when the article discusses that university/programme.
Avoid forcing the same anchor text into every article.
Do not build huge footer link farms.
Use contextual links where the user would naturally want the next answer.

create_news_only_when: There is a real current event, official admission update, result, regulatory update or meaningful university announcement.
do_not: Create daily low-value news just for freshness.
Create multiple pages from the same announcement.

hard_fail_conditions: Unverified current fee presented as fact

mobile: Tables become controlled scroll containers or cards.
Next-step links are visible but not intrusive.
Do not fill the first screen with popups.
performance: Reserve image dimensions to avoid layout shift.
Avoid unnecessary client-side rendering for SEO-critical text.
Keep structured data server-renderable where the current architecture allows.

qa_before_phase_8: Specialisation pages are generated only from verified specialisation data.
No thin specialisation pages are indexed.
Each indexed specialisation page has unique useful content.
Actual university-specific electives are distinguished from common explanatory content.
Articles have one clear search intent.
No major article cannibalises a course pillar, specialisation or university-course page.
Sources and verification dates are present where required.
lovable_prompt:
PHASE 6–7 — SPECIALISATION PAGES + SUPPORTING CONTENT CLUSTER

Implement the attached Phase 6–7 JSON.

This is a combined implementation of TWO layers:

PHASE 6 = dedicated specialisation pages.
PHASE 7 = supporting blogs/guides/articles/news architecture.

IMPORTANT:
1. Preserve all existing Phase 1–5 work.
2. Do not delete or rewrite good existing university-course, course-pillar or comparison content.
3. Do not change existing canonical URLs unless the JSON explicitly defines the new canonical route.
4. Build a reusable data-driven specialisation template.
5. Extract specialisations ONLY from verified university-course data.
6. Do not invent specialisations or electives.
7. Common curriculum explanation is allowed, but actual subjects/electives must remain university-specific and clearly labelled.
8. A specialisation page must contain substantial unique value; do not create thin pages for every keyword variation.
9. If a specialisation does not meet the quality/indexation threshold, keep it as a course-level navigation/filter rather than creating an indexable thin page.
10. Every specialisation page must show which universities actually offer it.
11. University availability must come from the verified programme data layer.
12. Every specialisation page must link to exact university-course pages.
13. Every relevant university-course page should link back to its specialisation page.
14. Course pillars should link to relevant specialisations.
15. Keep comparison links connected to the specialisation decision journey.
16. Build the supporting content system around real search intent, not keyword permutations.
17. Every blog/article must have one primary intent and a distinct role in the architecture.
18. Do not copy competitor content. Competitor pages can only be used for gap/intent analysis.
19. Official university/regulator sources are the factual authority.
20. Do not invent fees, curriculum, electives, recognition, rankings, placement percentages or salaries.
21. Add source and last-verified handling for dynamic facts.
22. Use contextual Next Step navigation instead of aggressive repeated CTAs.
23. Do not create fake news or publish thin articles merely to increase page count.
24. Apply the anti-cannibalisation rules in this JSON.
25. Keep mobile UX clean and prevent body-level horizontal overflow.
26. Preserve existing analytics, routing, SEO infrastructure and working functionality.

SPECIALISATION URL RULE:
Use:
 /online-courses/{course}/{specialisation}

Only index a specialisation URL when it has sufficient unique content and verified programme availability.

After implementation, provide a report containing:
- specialisations discovered
- specialisation pages created
- specialisations intentionally NOT indexed and why
- universities mapped to each specialisation
- university-course links verified
- article/content types created
- cannibalisation issues found
- duplicate content removed/prevented
- source/verification coverage
- SEO/canonical/schema audit
- mobile QA
- files/components changed
- anything requiring manual review

This is PHASE 6–7 ONLY. Do not implement Phase 8.
